In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage`, the check for fine-grained permissions incorrectly allows a user with only the `view` scope on all groups to be considered as having management permissions, which should require the `manage` scope.

In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`, the resource's internal UUID (`groupResource.getId()`) is incorrectly used to check permissions and is added to the returned set, instead of the group ID which is stored in the resource's name (`groupResource.getName()`).

In `GroupPermissionsV2.canMapRoles` and `canManageGroupMembership`, the logic was changed from `if (canManage(user))` to `if (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS))`, which is not equivalent and fails to grant permission if a user has fine-grained `manage` permission on a user but not the broad `manage-users` role.

In `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.onBefore`, `ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse` is called within a `try-with-resources` block that manages the same `Response` object, which will cause an error because the response is closed twice.

In `VerifyMessageProperties.java`, the `santizeAnchors` method modifies the string it is iterating over with a `Matcher`, which will cause the matcher to behave unpredictably as its internal state becomes out of sync with the modified string.

In `VerifyMessageProperties.java`, the `santizeAnchors` method incorrectly assumes that anchor tags will appear in the same order in both the original and translated strings, which will cause it to fail on valid translations that reorder phrases.

In `js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties` and `js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties`, the `error-invalid-multivalued-size` message format was changed to use Java's `MessageFormat` `choice` syntax, which is not compatible with the JavaScript i18n libraries used by these applications and will break pluralization.
In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_sk.properties`, the `impersonateTitleHtml` key is modified to have an unclosed `<strong>` tag, resulting in malformed HTML.

In `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties` and `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties`, the values for `totpStep1` and `loginTotpStep1` respectively are in Italian, not Lithuanian.
In `AccessTokenContext.java`, the constructor has a copy-paste error in a null check, causing it to check `grantType` for nullity twice while failing to check `rawTokenId`.

In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java`, the methods `getShortcutByGrantType` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut` are not thread-safe when dynamically updating the grant-to-shortcut maps, which can lead to an inconsistent state if new grant type providers are deployed at runtime.

In `AssertEvents.java`, the `isAccessTokenId` matcher is incorrect as it uses the wrong indices to extract the grant type shortcut and has inverted logic that would cause tests to fail on a correct match.

In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, calling `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking if the optional is present will throw a `NoSuchElementException` if the user does not have a recovery code credential.

In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials`, deserialization failure of recovery codes is only logged and does not propagate the error, which could lead to an incomplete set of credentials being returned.

In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid`, deserialization failure of recovery keys is only logged and the method returns false, which is indistinguishable from a failed validation and might be misleading.

The new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` in `GroupTest.java` has a race condition because the main thread does not wait for the background reader thread to complete before checking for exceptions, which could lead to the test passing incorrectly if an exception occurs in the reader thread after the assertion has been checked.
https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua: In `paginator.py`, the base `Paginator.get_result` method is modified to allow a negative `offset` when `cursor.is_prev` is true, which will cause a `ValueError` when slicing the queryset as Django's ORM does not support negative indexing.

In `paginator.py`, the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` method will raise a `ValueError` by attempting to slice a queryset with a negative `start_offset`, as this operation is not supported by the Django ORM.

In `paginator.py`, the logic for trimming extra results in `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` incorrectly compares the result count to `offset + limit + extra`, which is a slice boundary index, not an expected item count.

The `zunionstore` calls in `add-buffer.lua` are missing the `AGGREGATE` option, causing scores of overlapping elements to be summed by default, which will corrupt the timestamp-based scores and break the time-based eviction logic.

The batch insertion in `process_spans` does not cap the size of the sorted set, while the single-span insertion path in the Lua script does, and the safety check in `_load_segment_data` that previously dropped oversized segments has been removed, creating a risk of uncontrolled memory growth in both Redis and the consumer.

The `process_batch` function in `factory.py` directly accesses `val["end_timestamp_precise"]`, which will raise a `KeyError` and crash the consumer if it processes a message produced before this change that does not contain this field.
The function `_is_error_focused_query` uses a simple substring check for `event.type:error`, which is not robust enough and can incorrectly identify queries for upsampling.

The function `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` incorrectly returns `False` for an empty `project_ids` list, which prevents upsampling from being applied when a user has selected 'All Projects' in their filter.

The `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` test helper uses overly broad `except Exception: pass` blocks, which will silently swallow all errors during data extraction and prevent test failures on malformed test data.
https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull: The security check that validates the installing user against the authenticated user is bypassed if the installation webhook has not yet been processed, creating a race condition that undermines the security enhancement.
The call to `get_user_info` in `OAuthLoginView` is not within a try/except block, which will cause an unhandled exception and a 500 error if the GitHub API request fails.

The code accesses `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` without validation, which will raise a `KeyError` and result in a 500 error if the webhook payload that created the integration metadata had an unexpected structure.

In `OAuthLoginView`, the return value of `safe_urlopen` is not checked for `None` before being used, which will cause an `AttributeError` that is then obscured by a broad `except Exception` block, hiding the root cause of the failure.
https://github.com/ai-code-review-evalua: In `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, the static method `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` on `PRCommentWorkflow` incorrectly calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title()`, which does not exist; this method is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` and will cause an `AttributeError` at runtime.

In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, the `fetch_error_details` function incorrectly uses `zip(error_ids, events.values())` to map error IDs to event data, which is unreliable as the order of `dict.values()` is not guaranteed to correspond to the order of `error_ids`, leading to mismatched data.

In `static/app/views/dashboards/widgetCard/chart.tsx`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature is enabled, the new `TableWidgetVisualization` component is rendered with static, empty data instead of the actual `tableResults`, which will cause an empty table to be displayed.
https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/pull: In `SpanFlusher.join`, the loop that waits for child processes to exit will `break` prematurely if the timeout deadline is reached for one process, causing any subsequent processes to be neither waited for nor terminated.

In `SpanFlusher.join`, a child process is unconditionally terminated after the wait loop, even if it has already exited gracefully, because `process.terminate()` is called without checking if `process.is_alive()` is true.

In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, the call to `process.kill()` is only guarded against `ValueError` and `AttributeError`, but it can raise an unhandled `ProcessLookupError` (on POSIX) if the process has already died, which would crash the consumer.
The `AssignmentSource.from_dict` method does not deserialize datetime strings from the `queued` field, causing it to fail when processing data from a Celery task.
The `sync_status_outbound` method signature incorrectly uses `AssignmentSource` for a parameter that should represent the source of a status change, not an assignment.

In `get_monitor_environment_context`, a local `config` dictionary is created and modified, but the function returns the original unmodified `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the modified local variable.

In `try_incident_threshold`, when a monitor first enters a failed state, the code loops through all historical check-ins that contributed to the failure and creates a separate issue occurrence for each, which will generate multiple redundant events for a single incident creation.

In `create_incident_occurrence`, the event `timestamp` and occurrence `detection_time` are set to the processing time (`datetime.now()`), not the time of the actual failed check-in, which can make the event's timestamp inaccurate if there is a delay in processing.
The worker shutdown mechanism in `FixedQueuePool` is broken and will not terminate workers gracefully.
The test `test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling` incorrectly asserts that offsets are not committed after a processing error, which contradicts the worker's "skip-on-error" implementation.
The `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` class inherits from the abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` but does not implement its abstract methods, which will cause a `TypeError` at runtime.

In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, `PriorityLevel(new_status)` will raise a `ValueError` because it attempts to cast a `DetectorPriorityLevel` enum to a `PriorityLevel` enum, but their underlying integer values are not compatible.

In `test_state_results_multi_group`, the expected `IssueOccurrence` for `group_2` is built with a hardcoded value of `6`, but the input data packet provides a value of `10`, making the test assertion incorrect.
